fact: 865–868 MHz is licence-exempt for short range devices. For tracking, tracing and data acquisition devices: at most 500 mW e.r.p., channels up to 200 kHz, transmitting at most 2.5% of the time (10% for network access points), adaptive power control, and type-approved equipment.
source: DoT, Use of Low Power Equipment in the Frequency Band 865–868 MHz for Short Range Devices (Exemption from Licence) Rules, 2021 (G.S.R. 853(E)), Table II and rule 5; in DoT's compilation of subordinate legislation

fact: The 2.4 GHz band used by ESP-NOW is licence-exempt in India.
source: DoT notification G.S.R. 45(E), 28 January 2005, rule 3; in DoT's compilation of subordinate legislation

fact: The SX1276's maximum transmit power is +20 dBm (100 mW). Time on air follows Semtech's published formula, used in protocol.py.
source: Semtech SX1276 product page (links the datasheet)

fact: ESP-NOW carries up to 250 bytes per packet (v1) or 1470 bytes (v2). At most 20 paired peers, 17 of them encrypted. Broadcast and unencrypted packets are received without pairing. Encryption uses CCMP.
ESP-NOW with built-in antennas: about 150 m reliable, about 60% delivery at 300 m in an open field, and about 100% to 450 m in long-range mode. Not measured by us.
source: Espressif developer blog, "ESP-NOW for outdoor applications" (community authors, University of Žilina)

fact: HD44780 LCD controllers store only 8 custom characters.
500 m–1 km range at SF9 in dense Indian cities (Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore) for an SX1276 at +20 dBm with simple antennas. Our assumed 800 m range sits inside it.
source: Zbotic, SX1276 LoRa module range, sensitivity and spreading factor guide
